summary: First-run test of Jeana Marie's Kitchen Club. Ran 32 pytest cases across feature flags, auth, recipes, redeem, admin CSV/JSON export (7 entities x 2 formats = 14), flag gating, Stripe, and branding logo. Result: 31/32 backend passing (96.9%) after fixing a test-only email-case comparison. One CRITICAL business bug found: per-IP login rate limiter does NOT trigger behind Kubernetes ingress because request.client.host alternates between multiple ingress proxy IPs (verified 10.49.139.194 vs 10.49.134.136). Frontend: landing page loads with Recipe Book Stack SVG logo, brand text, hero, 3 free sample recipes CTA; admin login lands on /admin with all 8 tabs (Recipes, Printables, Codes, Families, Analytics, Flags, Branding, Export); mobile 375x812 has no horizontal overflow; redeem page reachable; register form present.

critical.issue: Rate limit (5 failed logins per IP+email / 5min) is INEFFECTIVE behind K8s ingress. request.client.host alternates between ingress proxy IPs so the sliding-window bucket never fills. 7 consecutive bad logins all returned 401. Fix: derive real client IP from X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP header (first value), fall back to request.client.host.

minor.issue: Route is POST-only; UI/docs may imply PUT. Test handles both. Consider accepting PUT for RESTful uploads.
Server lowercases email silently; returned user.email differs from input case. Consider returning original case OR documenting the lowercase-normalize behavior.

action_items: Fix rate limiter to use X-Forwarded-For to obtain real client IP (critical for brute-force protection on /auth/login, /auth/register, /auth/forgot-password, /auth/reset-password).
Consider adding data-testid attributes to Landing hero CTAs, register form fields, admin tab buttons for more robust future automation (currently we rely on text and structural selectors).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~780 lines - approaching split threshold. Consider splitting into routers/auth.py, routers/recipes.py, routers/admin.py, routers/payments.py, routers/files.py for maintainability.

In-memory rate-limit dict (_rate_buckets) is single-worker only. If backend scales to workers>1 or replicas>1, rate limiting will fragment. Since uvicorn is --workers 1 today, it is acceptable, but note in code.
download_file accepts token via ?auth= query param - exposes tokens in server logs / referrer headers. Consider short-lived signed URLs instead.
checkout endpoint uses _sync_db inside an async request handler; blocks event loop briefly. Prefer async db.payment_transactions.insert_one.
stripe checkout catches only InvalidRequestError; other stripe errors will 500 without a friendly message.
Reset password does not invalidate existing JWTs; a compromised token remains valid until expiry (30 days). Consider bumping a per-user token_version claim.
get_flags is called on every /files/upload and /journal write - fine for now but consider LRU-caching for hot paths.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py runs in ~10s and covers all critical flows. The one FAILING test is TestAuth::test_login_rate_limit which reveals a REAL production security bug (rate limiter ineffective behind ingress). If main agent fixes rate_limit to use X-Forwarded-For header, re-run pytest and this test will pass. Flags test uses PUT /api/admin/flags with the full flags dict; make sure future flag additions are non-breaking. Frontend admin tabs are: Recipes/Printables/Codes/Families/Analytics/Flags/Branding/Export - all render.
rca of the issue: Rate limit key = f'login:{request.client.host}:{email}'. Behind K8s ingress-nginx, request.client.host is the reverse-proxy pod IP, and there are multiple proxy pods that round-robin (observed 10.49.134.136 and 10.49.139.194 in backend access logs during 7 consecutive requests from a single curl loop). Because each request hits a different bucket key, the per-key counter never reaches the max_hits=5 threshold. Reproduction: `for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"x@y.com","password":"bad"}'; done` -> all 401, none 429. Mitigation: replace `request.client.host` with a helper `def real_ip(request): return (request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') or request.headers.get('x-real-ip') or (request.client.host if request.client else '')).split(',')[0].strip()` and use that for all rate_limit keys.
